description: The self-heal restart has NO backoff / circuit-breaker, so under a PERSISTENT failure it becomes a restart storm that reproduces the exact quota-burn the author documents as the project's main hazard (spec 2026-06-30-gig-earn-core-recipe-design.md:53-56 'I over-restarted the core ... burned the weekly quota to 96%'). gig-healthcheck.sh restarts on every DEAD detection (lines 16-17) with no counter and no escalating delay; launchd re-invokes it every 300s (ai.anicca.gig-core-healthcheck.plist:7 StartInterval 300). If claude cannot start (quota exhausted / auth lapsed), the detached tmux command (gig-cli.sh:34-35) exits and the session dies, so the next healthcheck sees DEAD and restarts again — spawning a fresh headless `claude` process every ~5 minutes indefinitely (~288/day), each consuming subscription budget and deepening the very quota exhaustion that caused the failure. The task's pass condition is 'self-heal ... WITHOUT a pathological loop'; an unbounded restart-spawn loop under persistent failure is that pathology.
fix: Add a restart counter + exponential backoff persisted to disk (e.g. ~/gig/.restart-count with a timestamp window), and stop restarting after N consecutive failures within a window, logging a single STALLED line instead of re-spawning. This directly prevents the documented quota-burn.
